name: kbd
title: Kbd
description: A keyboard key or shortcut hint, styled from the semantic tokens.
docs: ## When to use - A shortcut hinted next to a command: search, save, new item. - A key the user should press in a flow: `Tab`, `Esc`, `↑ ↓`. - Inside a `tooltip` or a `dropdown-menu` item, where space is short. ## When not to use - A key that is part of running text. Write it in prose; a pill interrupts the sentence. - A button that runs a command. A `kbd` is a label, not a control — it has no keyboard path and no press state. - Long sequences of more than three keys. Put the shortcut in a table instead. ## Installation ```bash npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/kbd ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Kbd, KbdGroup } from "@/components/cadence/kbd/kbd"; export function ShortcutHint() { return ( Search ⌘K ); } ``` ## Examples ### Single key ```tsx Esc ``` ### A combination `KbdGroup` renders the keys with one gap between them and keeps the sequence together for screen readers. ```tsx Ctrl Shift P ``` ### Inside a tooltip A `Kbd` inside `data-slot="tooltip-content"` inverts its colours automatically, so the hint stays legible on the tooltip surface. ```tsx Save ⌘S ``` ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | ---------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | | `Kbd` | native `kbd` props | One key. `data-slot="kbd"`. | | `KbdGroup` | native `kbd` props | Wraps several keys with `data-slot="kbd-group"`. | ## Motion contract No motion (T0). A key hint is a label; it must not pulse or slide while the user is reading it. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | ## Accessibility - Renders a real `` element, which assistive technology reports as keyboard input — the same information a sighted user reads from the key shape. - The shortcut is text, so it survives every reduced-motion mode and every colour theme. - If a hint is icon-only, put the key name in `aria-label` on the `Kbd`. - Do not attach `tabIndex`; a shortcut hint is not focusable. ## Notes for AI - Use the platform's own glyphs (`⌘`, `⇧`, `↵`) rather than words, and keep one `Kbd` per physical key. - If the shortcut is a live command, render a `button` and put the `Kbd` inside it.
